utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, could you continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Examined by MISS HOLLIS, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated, Mrs. Ramic. You are still under oath, the oath that you took yesterday. You may be seated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could turn off one of those microphones and, Mrs. Ramic, if you could sit back a bit from the microphone? Thank you. Mrs. Ramic, when we finished yesterday you had indicated that after the events that occurred in the military barracks you a few days later went to your village to visit your brother and after some time you came back again to your home in Prijedor. Do you recall your home being searched after your return to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the people who searched your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milorad Kicanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know Milorad Kicanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we had worked together in the Auto Transport Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he explain to you why your home was being searched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he said nothing. He only said, "I need to search your home".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything taken from your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he just threw things around, took everything from the wardrobe, searched everything and then left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after this search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I was standing in the corridor on his way out from the bedroom, he knocked me down and raped me in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he threaten you in any way after the rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if I told about this to anybody he would come back and kill me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day after this search were you again taken to the police department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Strika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know Strika?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he had been on duty at the bus station and travelled with me when we went from Dubica. Sometimes he got on the bus sometimes in Donji Milanovac sometimes in Gornji. That is how we knew him as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you transported to the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a green Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you on that trip to the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He cursed me and mentioned the derogatory names and we should all be killed since we do not want to be controlled by Serbian authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were at the police department did you see any Muslims there that you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Faruk Rizvic and his workman, Osman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their condition when you saw them at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in a bad condition. They were covered with blood. Their clothes were torn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When had you last seen Faruk prior to that day in the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had seen him one day prior to that time during the search.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him that day who was with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His workman, Osman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said this man's name is Faruk or Farud?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Faruk Rizvic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After you saw Faruk were you taken to a room at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they took us to a room called "buhara".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of this room to which you were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all covered with blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you in this room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko Boronja who had worked in Kripo came in with two soldiers in camouflage uniforms and with masks on their faces. You could not see who they were and then I was raped again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were raped were you also beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Ramic, at this time after the things that had occurred to you over the last few days, what was your emotional and mental state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Horrible, very, very bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this last rape at the police station were you taken to Keraterm from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Strika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how long you were held at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I know when they brought me to the guard house at the entrance they took me to the gate where I saw about 2,000 people in two rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were being held at Keraterm, did you see any of the detainees that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the first door, in the first room, I saw Faruk Rizvic, his workman Osman, Feho Ramic, Halid Nezirovic and a lot of other people I knew because I cannot remember, but most of them were known to me. In the second room, when I saw my brother, Suad Ramic, and my nephew, Fadil Softic, and (indecipherable), then I was sick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of these people that you saw there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had -- they were all beaten up, exhausted, covered with blood. Their clothes were torn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Ramic, while you were held at Keraterm did you see any detainees there who were beaten or injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a guard who was a stranger came and took me to the guard house and 10 minutes after that, I cannot quite remember how many, Zigic, the taxi driver, Zoran Zigic, followed by someone who called him Nedeljko, was called Nedeljko, they brought me to the area behind the guard house. I could not recognise who was who and what they looked like. When they knocked me down and when Zigic took out the knife and started to stab people, I started vomiting and I lost consciousness and I do not know anything what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Keraterm camp were you then taken to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it who took you to the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Policeman Bojic, the son of the forester, the ranger, forest ranger, from Bojici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Bojic's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you held at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that on 3rd August we left so we stayed there until 3rd August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what building were you held while you were at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the building where the restaurant is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take the pointer on that table and point to the building in which you were held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that because I experienced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the side of your console there, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At this entrance, the room right next to this entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the smaller building across from the long red building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would be seated, please? While you were held in that restaurant building during the night, were you held on the first floor or on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the first floor, the second room to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a woman named Hasiba Harambasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the same room that she was in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the day where were you held in the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Downstairs in the restaurant. As you go into the restaurant on the left-hand side, we were sitting at a table there, all the women there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were in the big room where the food was served?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the camp personnel, had you known them before you came to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did know some of them, but others I did not, but I did know most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are the ones that you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladjo Krkan, Mladen Radic, because he had several names, some people called him "Mladjo", others "Mlado", but his real name is Mladen Radic, Zeljko, Drago Prcac, Nedeljko, Pop, Rade, Brk, Stole, Ckalja, Dragenko and a couple of others. There are more of them, but I cannot remember at this moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew all of these people before you came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ones that you just named you knew before you came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a man named Zeljko, do you know what his last name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko Meagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guards and other camp personnel who worked at the camp, how did they dress?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were dressed in camouflage uniforms, or some former JNA uniforms, or in civilian clothes, but most of them wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the camp were you ever required to perform work duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of duties were you required to perform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to clean the toilets, the rooms upstairs, or go to the separation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perform any duties in the restaurant area itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We washed the dishes and handed out the meals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you would clean the rooms did that include rooms on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever find anything unusual as far as objects in those rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you find?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We used to find batons, a piece of cable, copper wires pushed through hose, pieces of wood, iron rods, square iron rods, aluminium pieces, and then there was led on top. It was all bloody. We had to clean that and hand it over to the Commander's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of those rooms when you cleaned them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were bloody. We used to find teeth, hair, pieces of human flesh, clothes, shoes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the camp at Omarska, did you ever see corpses there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where would you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between the big workshop where men were held, where they came out of to go to lunch, and in the area between that building and the hedge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see what was done with those bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They used to come with a small lorry, a yellow lorry, which had a long body, and they would take the dead bodies in the direction behind the white house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I ask you to enquire about the hedge? We have not heard of the hedge before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): You mentioned a hedge. Where was this hedge located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The hedge was to the left of the white house. There was a lawn there and the hedge was -- and the dead bodies were placed in front of that hedge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could ask you, please, what I am going to ask you to do will be to leave where you are sitting, come around to the model and for the Court point out where this hedge was located near the white house. If you could do that now, please? You can take off your headphones and just come around and point to where it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far -- if you could put on the headphones -- along there did that hedge run?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a long one, but we did not pay much attention, but this is where the hedge was and this is where the dead bodies were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did the hedge run parallel to the white house and the small red building? Point in the direction in which the hedge was growing. Is it long-wise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a long hedge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It ran from that location you pointed how far toward the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did not go towards the white house. The hedge was on this side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, we could go around the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the hedge was closer to that small red building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes it was closer to the red building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you could resume your seat? To your knowledge, this yellow truck that you talked about, was this truck used for anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They brought food in on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an occasion when you saw bodies taken away in a larger truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recall about that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When a guard came to pick us up to take us down there, we came to the glass on the way out of the staircase, suddenly they returned us, they took us back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had you seen before they took you back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had seen the yellow lorry and machine for loading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big was this truck that you saw on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was big, bigger than the yellow lorry I referred to earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen similar trucks like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please repeat, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Prior to seeing this truck, had you seen trucks that were similar to this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of trucks were these?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were similar to the Mann, Fap which is a Yugoslav factory or TAM which is a Slovenia factory of lorries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what those types of trucks were used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They used them for public transportation, for the transportation of gravel, wood, etc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard any sounds or unusual activity the night before you saw this truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had heard moans, screams and the noise, the noise of something like a fence being broken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean "something like a fence being broken"? What kind of noise is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As if you were breaking something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later that morning, after you had been told to go back to your room, were you brought down to the restaurant area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any unusual activity at the white house that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw men being taken out of the white house and then, using a hose, forced them to strip, beat them on the pista, there were people facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were held at Omarska were other women held there with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea of the number of women who were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 36 Muslim women and two Serbian women and two Croat women -- three Croat, three Catholic women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there at Omarska do you recall an occasion when two women named Edna Dautovic and Sadeta Medunjanin were taken from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you remember about that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember clearly because that day on 20th a guard had a birthday, he said. On 20th July at half past 10 they came and took away Sadeta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where they were taken when they were taken from the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We rushed out, a couple of us, we went to the place where there was a bath tub and a toilet and, of course, when we saw we were shocked because we were expecting that to happen to us every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you looked out of that window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Out of the window I saw Zeljko Meagic and Mirko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Mirko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember his surname. He had a beard. Babic, yes, Babic was his surname. Then we saw the bus with people being taken to it and it said, "Unatrans Bihac" on the bus and then it said, "Private business, owner Seselj".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw people being put on that bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I saw that we were all frightened, but since Tidza had remained behind, because her brother had been called out, she remained with us and watched that incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the people were loaded on the bus. Did you recognise any of the people loaded on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever actually see Sadeta or Edna being put on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when they took them away, they said they would be exchanged in Bihac. As soon as they got on the bus, we went back to our room and Tidza remained behind and then heard her brother's name being called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without mentioning the names of any women, I would ask you if during the time you were at Omarska, during the night, any women were called out of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would call the women out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladjo, Drago Prcac, Zeljko Meagic, Nedelkjo Grabovac or Pop, fat, heavily built with a moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again without mentioning the names, did any of the women who were called out ever tell you what had happened to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we never told each other what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you yourself called out of the room at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did this happen to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it who called you out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladjo, Mladen Radic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the man you also referred to as "Krkan"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this man would called you out of the room where would he take you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He would take me downstairs to the first room next to the staircase on the way to the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he took you down there to this room what did he do to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Raped me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten by him as well as raped by him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once only as I was going out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of the other camp guards or personnel when you were being taken to that room or back from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Zeljko Meagic while I was coming out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you saw Zeljko Meagic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He only slapped me in the face and said, "You, whore, scram to your room".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of the treatment to you in the camp at Omarska and what had happened to you previously, did you eventually come to a point where you contemplated trying to find a way to commit suicide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone talk to you about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Biba and Zlata, they did, and they were crying, "No, please do not; we shall survive, we shall live, to tell the truth".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of the rapes that were done to you, did you have continuing medical problems after you left the camp and after you left Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those medical problems eventually result in your having surgery to remove your uterus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left the Omarska camp where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Prijedor -- sorry, to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Trnopolje you went back to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until January 13th '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the conditions like for you in Prijedor during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bad. We could not go out. We could not buy anything. If you went out, somebody beat you because many people knew you, so they would take you to the MUP and give you beating, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to leave Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I still wonder, is it possible that I am still alive?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to pay someone to get you out of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how much you had to pay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall that and I would not say that. The important thing is that life was dear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you last see your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 10 days before I was taken to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard anything from him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing. I only know that we saw each other that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you made attempts to find him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had any success at all in determining what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not learn anything.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No cross-examination, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mrs. Ramic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Ramic, you are free to go. You are free to leave. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may leave now. The usher will help you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, will you call the next witness? Mr. Niemann, we have a selection today.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have two motions at this time we would like to be heard. They involve matters that are coming up. We will need to do those in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How long do you anticipate it will take to consider those motions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It should be fairly quickly, your Honour. They deal with issues regarding witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. We will stand in recess for approximately 10 minutes, the time required to convert this to a closed session. Is there any objection from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. We will stand in recess for 10 minutes and then we will return in closed session. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The next witness is Emir Beganovic. EMIR BEGANOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being given to you? Read that oath and take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am 41.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your occupation before the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had private restaurant business and together with my wife I had florist shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many restaurants or cafes did you own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three, and the fourth one was the florist shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were your businesses located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two of them on the Esada Midzica Street, the third restaurant was on Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that you were well known locally as a successful businessman in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of Prijedor did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 1990 I lived in the old town, in Stari Grad, until I built myself a flat in Salamica Street and I moved then there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the elections of 1990 and before the outbreak of the actual conflict in 1992, did increasing tensions develop between Serbs and Muslims in the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was growing after the elections, after the party election the tensions began to grow, but it was not as strongly felt as when the conflict in Croatia broke out. When that conflict broke out, then the tensions began to mount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that time had people in Prijedor tended to distinguish between who was Muslim and who was Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, by physical appearance one could not distinguish between them, only if we knew each other, if we knew who was a Muslim, who was a Croat, who was a Serb, but there was no difference whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have Serb friends as well as Muslim friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at the present time after this war when I look back, I find that I had more friends among the Serbs than among the Muslims, I mean, family friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the tensions you spoke of increased before the outbreak of the conflict, did you become involved with a group in Prijedor town that was interested in promoting peace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I joined the League for Peace, and I was on its steering committee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the establishment of the League for Peace result from any particular incident or was it a response to the general situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was spontaneous. I aspired to having all options open in Prijedor just to avoid war, and we thought that regardless of what Party who had voted for ought to join us, and simply show the leadership of the first and the second and third Party that the people was not for war -- that people were not for war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when was the League established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The League was established in '91, sometime towards the end of '91, I cannot remember the month exactly. I believe it was November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the primary organiser of the League?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Primary organiser was Dr. Esad Sadikovic, called "Eso".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dr. Sadikovic a medical doctor who had previously worked with the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there persons of all nationalities on the steering committee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the League for Peace have any connection with any political group or any other peace group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The purpose of the group was to unite people in Prijedor in the hope of avoiding any inter-ethnic conflicts or tensions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What steps did the League for Peace take in this effort to promote inter-ethnic harmony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we mostly organised concerts in public, public concerts in the centre of the town. We tried to organise concerts in the beginning while we still could get permission from the local SUP. We had our meetings in public. Anybody was admitted, whoever wanted to come. But later on things began to be more complex. The SUP refused to give us permission to organise concerts, and they stopped permitting us to rent out a hall for our meetings. It just dwindled and gradually faded out spontaneously because it had no possibilities of continuing its activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period in which the League was able to obtain permission to hold concerts, how many people attended those concerts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was never a concert attended by less than 7,000 or 8,000 or 10,000 people even.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there speeches or messages of peace during the concerts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All the addresses, all the speeches were serving the purpose of peace. There were no speeches actually, there were political messages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, the translation says "there were political messages". What kind of messages were delivered during the concerts the League for Peace conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no, not political messages, messages for peace, peace messages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eventually the League for Peace disbanded because of obstruction from the authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when did the League for Peace conclude its efforts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should say towards the end of February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that at a time of increasing tensions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The tensions were increasing from one day to another at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you send your family out of the area for safety?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I sent them to their relatives in Croatia, in Istria.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did your family leave the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they left on 12th March '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remained in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remained in Prijedor, and a few days later I moved to Dr. Esad Sadikovic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you concerned about what might happen in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was concerned. That was why I had moved my family away, but I could never dream that anything even remotely like what did happen could happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in Prijedor when the Serbs took power in a takeover on April 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the takeover did tensions mount?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, hour after hour the tension mounted with every hour, ever since the moment they took over the power on 29th April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at Dr. Sadikovic's house when the cleansing of Prijedor town began on May 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the windows of Dr. Sadikovic's house or from his terrace, were you able to see what was happening in Prijedor and, in particular, in Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you able to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see that Stari Grad was ablaze literally. I could even identify the position of my parent's house. I could see it on fire. Literally the whole of Stari Grad was aflame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Different kinds of uniforms, of different colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I guess they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear announcements over the radio about what Muslims should do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had the radio on and we listened, the warnings and instructions how people should behave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the radio messages instruct Muslims to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in the beginning they said we should merely stay partly in our houses, that nothing would happen. Then a little bit later on, perhaps after an hour or so, they said that all Muslims should put out white flags on their houses and if they did not have any flags, then perhaps bed linen, sheets or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we put out bed sheets on both sides of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "we put out bed sheets", who was in Dr. Sadikovic's house with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That morning there was my friend, Asif Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then at some point after you and Mr. Kapetanovic had hung the white sheets in response to the instructions on the radio, did he observe something that caused him great concern?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at a certain point he went to the terrace on the upper floor and saw that his business premises were on fire. It was a one-storeyed house on the ground floor, they had their business. On the upper floor they had a flat. I heard him scream. I asked him what was it and he said that his mother was in that flat upstairs, and that the flat was on fire, and I ran out. I could see the flames, perhaps as much as 20 metres high. The house was ablaze. It was literally all burning. Perhaps it took him some time to calm down, and he decided then to go and see what had happened to his mother. At that point I did not know what to do. So I decided to go with him. I could not really leave him to himself, because for the past few days he was suffering from kidneys and that was why he was in Eso's house, to treat his kidneys, and he could not, of course, go to the hospital because the hospital had already been taken over by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were outside were you confronted at some point by a Serb soldier and did you flee that soldier and run into the nearest Muslim house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The soldier came up and said, "Halt". We were some 50 metres away and I automatically said, "Asif, I am not going to wait for him, I am fleeing", and there was the wire of the house nearby -- there was a hedge of the house nearby and I jumped over that hedge, and then I heard three or four bursts of fire, but I was in the luck, I was not hit. Then I crawled behind that house to another house. I used to know people who lived around there. I knew it was a Muslim house. I knocked on the door and was flabbergasted when I saw another friend of mine, Saim Mesanovic who opened the door for me and let me in even though he was from a different part of the town, and that was his relative's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in that house was there another announcement on the radio that Muslims should put white ribbons or arm bands on their arms, form columns and go to the main square?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they said that all Muslims from that part of the town should come out and head for the town with white arm bands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and the other persons in the house do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once outside were you directed by Serb forces toward the area of the taller buildings in the town centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they directed us in the direction of the small marketplace. Then by Muharem Rujanovic Street, there were three skyscrapers in Prijedor and that is where they stopped, they directed us. There was a column of perhaps 1,000 to 2,000 people. I would not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the way did you see any corpses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the marketplace I went round a pile in which there were some four or five bodies, and then I happened to glance over the area of the marketplace and I saw another body lying there, and then I could not stand it any longer and I turned my head away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those bodies of civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached the area they directed you to, were there buses waiting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the buses were already there, parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Serb forces then begin to separate the men from women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they said that men over the age of 15 should stand, should move to one side, and children below the age of 15 and women should go to the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you board one of those buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you first taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, first they took us to the SUP and that is where the buses stopped, by the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So first to the police station in Prijedor town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the police station in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the bus remain there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not long, some 10 minutes or so, five or 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there guards on your bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were two or three perhaps. I remember that one had got off and entered the SUP building, probably to get instructions, and returned after a couple of minutes, and the bus continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have been referring to your bus. Were there other buses loaded with men and boys over the age of 15 along with your bus at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the relatively brief period of time at the Prijedor SUP, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken by JNA street. We came out of the JNA street to the tennis grounds, to Partizanska and then on towards Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that where did the buses go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before Tomasica they turned. I had never used that road before. Later on I learned that it was the road to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where your bus was taken, to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (11.30 a.m.) (Short Adjournment) (11.50 a.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Beganovic, before I discuss Omarska with you, I wanted to ask you a question about something you discussed earlier. You mentioned that the efforts of the League for Peace were obstructed by the authorities in Prijedor. Which authorities obstructed those efforts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian authorities in addition to the SDA Party. They had a great influence in the municipality and in the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it Serbian authorities rather than SDA which resisted the efforts of the League for Peace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned when you were discussing one of the routes taken in your description the street Marsala Tita. Was that Marsala Tita Street in Prijedor town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, until 30th May it was Marsala Tita Street, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you now about the places you were held in Omarska camp. Were you first held in a room in the restaurant building for one night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the model in front of you, can you use the pointer which is on the table to show us where the restaurant building is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The restaurant building is here. (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of the restaurant building were you initially held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The buses were parked here. We went through this entrance and we were put in this room here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the first night where were you held then, in what part of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was transferred to the pista, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there for about 10, 11 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the white house for a couple of nights after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I spent two nights there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that were you held on the upper floor of the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in room No. 15, as it was called. This is where you enter, roughly in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the later period of your confinement in Omarska, did you stay in a small room in the restaurant building and also for a short time in the small garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, two days and two nights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, how would you describe the general conditions of Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The general conditions are indescribable. I have no words to describe it. I do not know how to tell this to the honoured courtroom. Every minute we were upset, we were beaten, psychologically abused, starved, left without drink, without drinking, drinks -- simply it is impossible to describe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When would beatings of prisoners occur? During what sorts of activities by prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The worst was during the day they interrogated inmates in this building upstairs from the restaurant. 99 per cent of the people came back beaten up, and the nights were even more horrible. After their hours, work hours, at 5 o'clock they stopped interrogating. Then there were private visits by Serbian soldiers, guards, civilians. Whoever wanted to go there, go in, did so and looked for inmates, calling their names, surnames or nicknames. We were even taken by people who had never met us before. We lay down on our stomachs in the pista. They would simply come, "Give me two, give me three", "Here, take five, if you like". Simply, people were lying on their stomachs. Someone comes and kicks you, "Stand up, stand up, you and you and you". I do not know that anyone came back, any of those people came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were prisoners beaten on their way to the restaurant for their meal and on their way to use the toilet when they were permitted to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten on your way to the restaurant or on your way to use the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, regularly when I was in the group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also called out for special beatings, that is, individual beatings while you were in camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three times. However, the last couple of days in the camp I was called out every hour or two because of the blackmail because I was asked for money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic participate in one of the three beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who Dule Tadic was before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long before the war had you known who he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 10 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you happen to know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, by the force of circumstances. His arrival in Prijedor brought him to the area where I had my restaurant. He was known to create conflicts. He used to come with his karate people, so-called karate people. They were usually beaten in Prijedor when they came, but still they came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what area he lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him from -- I knew that he was from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you often go to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I had friends, relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you go to cafes in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also see Dule Tadic in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On several occasions, yes, in restaurants, in the streets. We did not greet each other. We were not friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be with friends who did know him and who did greet him when you passed in the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the 10 years that you mentioned, did you come to know who he was and to be easily able to recognise him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about the first two beatings that you mentioned, the first two times you were called out specially for beating. Did the first one take place during the period of time that you were on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at the time you were called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Half an hour prior to that time they put us in the restaurant room. It was bad weather and we were all put back into the restaurant room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the person who called you out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later find out who he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later I did. Other inmates told me that his name was Dragan, that he was a relative of Nedzo Delic, the well-known cafe owner, restaurant owner. He owned the restaurant Europa in Omarska and another restaurant called Europa II in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was Dragan dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was dressed in the grey olive uniform and he had a white military policeman's belt. He had a pistol and he had police batons on each side of his belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What nationality was Dragan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard in the camp that he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After calling you out of the restaurant building, did Dragan first take you to see someone whom you did know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he took me out at this semicircle. Nikica Janjic was standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you had a conflict of some sort with Nikica Janjic before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, about a year and a half before the outbreak of the war, I had a confrontation, I had a physical conflict with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that occur on an evening when you broke up a fight between Janjic and his girlfriend and then later intervened when he attacked one of your employees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Janjic tell you when you were brought to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, "See how times have changed? Tonight I am going to cut your throat".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that did they bring you back to the restaurant building for a short time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did bring me back for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then were you called out again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear the question. They took me to the pista. At the exit of the building Dragan started beating me with the baton on the head, on the neck, on the back, the upper part of my back. He kept hitting me in that area as we went to the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other prisoners called out and taken to the white house at approximately the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that I was followed by Terzic Sefik, Sefik Terzic, a well-known hairdresser from Prijedor, nicknamed "Kiki". Then they called out Asaf after me. Asaf was in the same restaurant where I was. Then Rezak Hukanovic, nicknamed "Dzigi", the three of them and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Rezak Hukanovic's occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rezak Hukanovic, he was a poet and an entertainment manager. Asaf Kapetanovic was also a well-known businessman in Prijedor and a rich man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that all three of these men were well-known and successful people in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were very well-known and successful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all three men Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you placed when you were taken to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was placed in the second room on the right. The other three were placed in the second room to the left, as far as I could assess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you were taken to the second room on the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They started beating me immediately, and Dragan and Nikica were the only people there with me. The other Serbian soldiers were on the other side where the other three were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Dragan and Nikica do to you in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat me, both of them. Dragan was hitting me with a baton. Nikica kicked me. I do not remember whether he used an object, whether he used an object to hit me, but he mostly kicked me. I tried to protect myself as much as I could using my hands, but occasionally I saw people coming from the other room. It was Saponja, the handball player from Prijedor. He used to be my friend. His parents, their wedding took place in my house, because they had just moved to Prijedor, they had not found a dwelling place yet. So his father and my father were very good friends. His mother borrowed my mother's dress to get married in. Others came in too, there was also the well-known murderer from before the war Zigic and then Duca, Dusko Knezevic. They came in from time to time carrying various objects. They also had some cables, electric cables, and with a ball on top of it welded on to the cable. I do not know how they made those devices, but they used these -- used everything that was available to beat us. But in this beating Dragan and Nikica were the main individuals who beat us, the others just came in from time to time to beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the beating continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an eternity, as far as I was concerned, but maybe about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point did they order you to lie down on the ground, on the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Dragan ordered me to lie down, to stretch out my arms, with my stomach facing the floor, but we knew, the inmates knew, that in many cases their spines were broken. I tried to resist not to lie down. I told them to kill me. I said I did not want to lie down. I refused to lie down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At one point there was something like a desk and a chair. I do not know how I found myself on that chair. As far as I remember, my left arm, my left arm was on the desk and at one point Nikica took out a knife about this size. I thought, because he had told me that he would cut my throat, that he had taken the knife in order to cut my throat. Almost automatically I started to lift my arm and I felt at that moment that a knife stabbed my hand and I still had still have the scar. The blood spurred out of the wound, spurted. At that point I lost consciousness and then I know that they took me out of that room. At that point the other three friends of mine were coming out of the other room and they took us out, out of the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were being beaten, could you tell what was happening to the other prisoners who had been called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We just heard screams and moans. I was not interested in others. I was in such a bad condition that I was not able to worry about others because my own life was at risk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the beating were you held in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us out and led us towards the pista, and at one point Zigic said, told us to bend down and to drink the water next to the kerb like dogs, and that we should behave like dogs and drink the water like dogs. We drank the water which we were glad to do because my throat was dry. At that moment those bad words had no meaning to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that were you returned to stay in the pista or were you taken back to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that the three of them were taken towards the pista, the restaurant. I was ordered by Dragan to go back to the white house. He started hitting me again on the way to the white house. He hit me a couple of times and then he threw me into the first room to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay there for that night and the following night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I stayed there that night until about 10.00 or 11.00 in the morning. Then they returned us, a whole group of us -- there were about 150 or 200 in the group -- to spend the night in the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were in the white house did a guard see you and comment on your condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I entered that room I saw there were about 10 or 12 young men in civilian clothes. We knew already that the room was assigned for so-called Muslim extremists who had attacked Prijedor, and we also knew that nobody would come alive out of that room. In the evening, about 8 or 9 o'clock, maybe 10.00, I cannot quite remember, a guard came up to the window. Slavko Ecimovic was there in prison, my friend from school and from childhood. He told him at one moment, "You say you did not attack Prijedor, look, look in your group, there is even a black man", and he had a flash light on and I knew that it was trained at me. As far as I could move, because my pain was horrible, I said, "I am not a black man. I have been here for 12 days in the pista. I was on the pista mostly and they came privately and beat me up". The man remained breathless and said, "Is it possible?" He went around through the door. He crouched next to me. He again directed his flash light at me. He said, "Mother fuckers, is it possible to beat up a man like they beat you up?" I saw that he was speaking, that he was honest about it. I said, I asked him if he could help me to be transferred to the pista, to the group that I belonged to because my life was at risk where I was, that those young men had come after me and I have no connection with them. He said that at that moment he could not promise anything, but he would try to transfer me, which he did. He came the following morning about 8.00 or 9.00 and visited me. I think his name was a Radenko. He left. He said he did not know nothing, he could not tell me anything that is concrete. So he came about 10.00, at 11 o'clock in the morning, he took me out and led me to the hangar. There were some wash basins there. He told me to wash. There was a mirror there and then everything became clear to me. I looked at myself in the mirror and I saw what I looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, what was the condition of the other prisoners in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Horrible, incredible, very similar to mine. There may have been worse cases than me. People could not move mostly. There were people who could not move a single centimetre without a moan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after you were transferred to room 15 was it before the second beating occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who called you out on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nikica Janjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day they took us out of room No. 15, all of us, because of a list that they were about to make. They were making some lists. We were on the lawn between the white house and the red house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Janjic take you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other Serb there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a guard Commander, Kvocka, and a guard. I know his nickname was Ckalja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other Serbs there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were always guards. They were just hanging around. We were not particularly interested to observe them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other Serb in the white house when Janjic took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was promised safety by Ckalja. It was really just a formality so that I could be dragged into the white house, because I said, "This is what they have done to me. The man wants to cut my throat". He says, "I guarantee your safety. Go in and have a word with him". So I knew that I had to go in, so I did. A small, skinny soldier, about 160 metres tall, with a jacket remained at the doorway with a bag, with a big bag on his back. It looked funny with an automatic rifle, and Nikica started beating me at the same moment. The other man was standing at the door to prevent me from fleeing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Nikica Janjic beat you in the white house on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first he kicked me with his feet, then beat me with hands. Then he took out his Colt pistol, and I always remembered what he told me, and began to beat me with the pistol handle on the head. My head was all swollen already, but he went on hitting me with that pistol and made holes in my head. Perhaps it was a good for me because the blood had already coagulated and was all so swollen, and perhaps all this coagulated blood then came out from the body through those wounds he inflicted at that moment. So perhaps that is how I can explain that my skull did not burst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did that beating continue for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It went on for a long time, 20 minutes perhaps. He was already tired. He was sweating. His shirt was wet with sweat and he was sweating all over. He was quite a big guy. So that at one point he stopped beating me. I asked him to listen to me, to bear up with me for a couple of minutes and then, if he wanted to, he could go on beating me or just do me any or, at any rate, finish with me. To my surprise, he agreed to talk to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you tell him or what did he tell you during that discussion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I told him as regards that conflict that we had before, and that I assumed the responsibility for it, yes, I had hit him, but now what he had done on those two occasions I thought that was a sufficient tit for tat and that I did not hold any grudges against him, not too much, and that he should either kill me or let me be, and to make his choice, to do what he wanted but, at any rate, to finish somehow with me. So he thought for a while and said, "I will let you live. I will not kill you". After that he started talking with me more and more. I could not speak any more. I remember as I asked him to take me out, but then he sent one of those lads who was standing with the automatic in the doorway to go and bring some water. He did, and let me drink water. I washed a little, that is, washed the blood off my face. He said thank my mother because she told me not to kill you. She made me swear that I would not kill you because you are an only son and she had an only son, and she advised him in this way. Perhaps this had taken the upper hand, this prevailed, and he did not kill me and he kept his word and did not come again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that did you continue to be held in room 15 and were you in room 15 when the third beating occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after this second beating was it before the third beating took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that too about two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time was it when you were called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was late in the afternoon, maybe, around 6 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who called you out or just hear a voice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only heard a voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the voice coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The voice came from the entrance, from the door of room No. 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After being called out did you leave the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you did what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw somewhere in the middle, halfway up the stairs Dragan standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, in a moment I am going to ask you to get up from the chair and point out on the model -- if you can wait just a moment I will have the roofs removed -- where you were when you were called out, where room 15 was. If the roofs could be removed from the models? Both roofs of the big building? Mr. Beganovic, I do not know if the cameras will be able to pick this up, but you will be able to read the numbers. If you can walk over to the model and both point what room you were in and then tell us what numbers are written there. You can remove your headphones for that and then return to your seat. Can you point to room 15, the area that comprised room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the numbers written on the floor of the area which comprised room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking loudly, can you tell us what those numbers are?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can barely hear the witness. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, if you can remember the numbers and turn to the microphone immediately behind you, the interpreters will be able to pick up what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Repeat the numbers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, can you repeat the numbers that are shown in room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B23, B8, and three times B7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you are looking at the model now, which way did you go to leave room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was lying in this corner, then here, here were the wash basins and I came out of this door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, and then went down the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Down the stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can take your seat again, Mr. Beganovic. Thank you. Mr. Beganovic, you said you saw Dragan; is that the same Dragan who had been involved in beating you before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again the military uniform with the white belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During those beatings when I was put in that room, one of the detainees had bandaged my head with some white cloth. I do not know what it was, a t-shirt or a shirt but, at any rate, it was a white rag to stop the bleeding, and that cloth had stuck to my head and just stayed there. I did not even try to remove it because it had all hardened already with the blood. So that I came out with this to face him, and he said, "What do you need that on your head for? You are not a Hodza, you sell flowers", and I had nothing to tell him in response. He told me to come down.
