utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he said, "You are not a Hodza, he was mocking the bandage on your head as if it was a turban?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went down the steps what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The moment I came down the stairs he started beating me, I think with a baton again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he push you or direct you to any particular part of the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He directed me towards the hangar, towards the inside of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the ground floor of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other Serbs there waiting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a group of soldiers wearing different kinds of clothes, but they were all military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, how many in this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I should say seven to 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dule Tadic a member of this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the group what did they do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I burst in among them and they simply at the same time started beating me as usual, beating with different objects, mostly with the feet, boots, those soldiers boots, also some sticks, some metal rods, some metal cables, with all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dule Tadic one of those actively involved in hitting and kicking you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what he was wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had the multi-coloured military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he was clean shaven or had a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he looked unkempt, like all of them rather unkempt, untidy a beard very untidy. He did not have a real beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he had some days growth of beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the beating continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It went on between 20 minutes and half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you lose consciousness during the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the hangar on the ground floor, no. I did upstairs when it was all over and when I went up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt to remain conscious during the beating for a particular reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because I realised that if I fainted I would never wake up again because they simply killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the beating continued where did you end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It ended, I ended up in the hall -- they were beating me and I fell among some pillars, if I recollect, I think they were white and red as if some markings to mark, to bind off a particular area where some work goes on so one cannot enter that area. So I was among those pillars somehow. I do not know how I got there. At one point I could not, I was not even trying to come out from amongst those pillars and then two came, approached me, I do not know who they were, I cannot remember, and they got me by my feet and hung me up by a cord.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was this -- the translation says they hung you up by a cord. What kind of a device was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really remember properly, whether it was plated but it was -- there was a canal nearby and I think that cord, that cable served to lift some weight, some engines or something like that. Some large and heavy object I think it served to lift those things up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you hanging there by your feet upside-down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not determine the time with any precision, but not long, several minutes, one minute, two, three, I do not remember exactly. At any rate at some point I felt that my feet had slid out and I fell down and at that moment I remember Dragan approached me again and asked if I knew who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you tell him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told him I did not know him, that I had never seen him in my life before, that I did not know who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you tell him you did not know who he was and that you had never seen him before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because it was a fact in the camp, it was a common fact in the camp that they never left alive those witnesses who might possibly recognise those guards who killed and tortured. Simply, they left no witnesses behind. I realised simply that it would be better for me to say that I did not know him, and even had I known him before I would have said that I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you told Dragan you had never seen him before, what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, "Take this one upstairs and bring me Senad Muslimovic".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go upstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I started upstairs. I reached the staircase. I did not even know that I did not have my sneakers on, and at one point they said, "Go back and fetch your sneakers." I said, "I don't need them", and Dragan sort of said: "You want me to fetch them for you? Come here." So what could I do? I had to go back and they started beating me again. How I managed to bend down and pick up those sneakers I do not know but I know I did. Then I climbed up the stairs and entered room 15, and when I was there I made may way to that corner where my place was and I fainted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long you lost consciousness for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how long I was unconscious, but from what my friends told me, those who washed me with water that brought it from the wash basin, several minutes, it was several minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you regained conscious, could you tell whether other prisoners were being beaten downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you able to hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard screams, screams that I had not known before. Until I arrived in that camp I had never heard such cries, such screams. They were human, but I could never imitate them. I remember I asked a friend Rizah Salas who helped me throughout my stay in the camp and at a point saved my life, if I was also letting out such screams, and he said: "We heard you, no, not even remotely like that."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the next couple of days did you find out who had been beaten downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the next couple of days after that did you learn who had been beaten downstairs and whose screams you had heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we learnt, I think the next day, that it was my friend Jasko, that Emir Karabasic was there who one day before had visited me in the 15 and then they had sent him to ask money from the inmates, to collect some money, and probably that was how he had managed to enter the room and reach me and be with me for a while and just patted me on the head and said: "Take care of yourself, don't worry you will get out", but he did not stay long. He went out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Jasko's last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those men from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, what injuries did you receive from the beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The injuries, they are both bodily and mental, but those physical injuries are worse. I have fractures on my head, my head was all pierced, was all in holes. My hand is injured. I cannot really use it and I think it is even thinner than my right one. Then my spine is hurt. My kidneys are injured, my leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive medical care for your injuries in camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, only in so far as the prisoners could help me. You mean whether I received any treatment after the camp?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, in Omarska itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was treatment amongst ourselves. We looked after one another. Dr. Eso, because my nose was all to the right and Eso managed to return it. How well he succeeded you can see for yourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Sadikovic have medical supplies with which to treat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no medicines or any supplies. From time to time he would go upstairs above the restaurant and there he tended, he looked after the Serb soldiers who came back from the front, those who were wounded, because people often inflicted wounds on themselves when cleaning their weapons. So he did go upstairs to treat them and then he would manage to get some pills or bandages and some powders. I remember him bringing some phials, some bottles. I think he used those powders to make something. He had one syringe and he used it for everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Dr. Sadikovic received medical supplies to treat Serb soldiers and smuggle whatever he could to help the Muslim prisoners who were injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it was very, very small quantities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your wounds become infected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of your wounds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The worst were head injuries, because that cloth, the bandage I had, it was on my head for about a month and it was all rotting and there were worms. Fortunately Dr. Eso noticed that and asked a guard to take me out when I was in this room above the restaurant and there was a water tap here, to go out and for about two days he kept begging me to go out and I did not dare because I was afraid that one of them would come and recognise me because there were rumours in the camp that I had succumbed. But he eventually did prevail upon me and I agreed. He said that I simply had to . So I agreed and he took me out to that tap and there for about an hour he was wetting it and managed to remove those bandages. There were worms in it. I did not know that. I learned that the next day and that was why he put pressure on me to wash it, I was to wash it off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did other prisoners have worms and infected wounds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite a number of cases. There were guys who had wounds on their backs or all over the body but, for instance, on the backs there were some chaps where two or three litres of pus would simply spurt out on the back. They had things like a balloon on their backs and it would finally burst. So there were quite a number of people who were still alive and yet from whom worms were coming out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you have mentioned Dr. Sadikovic on several occasions, both in connection with his efforts with the League for Peace and in the ways he attempted to treat Muslim prisoners. What happened to Dr. Sadikovic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 5th August he was with us all the time in this room above the restaurant where we stayed in this small room with 20 or 25 of us. On 5th August he was taken out, perhaps around 11 o'clock in the evening, it was night time, and before that at least on two occasions he had been taken out and brought back and he was told to take his things with him, although he had nothing. We had said goodbye to him on two occasions, and on the third occasion when he was called out he turned and said to us, "Fuck you all". That is what he told us, jokingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see or hear of Dr. Sadikovic again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came out from the camp in '93, in March, I heard from a relative, from Azo's relative that she had heard from three sides and from different Serb soldiers that he had been in the camp at Ric near Bihac and that he had personally treated them. However, after that I could not learn anything, even though I keep on enquiring but to no avail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, can you look and tell us if Dule Tadic is in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is, Serb garbage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please refrain from that language, if you would, and can you point out -- I know you pointed ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise to your Lordships. I could not stop myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have pointed to where he is sitting. Can you just tell us what he is wearing, please, or exactly where he is sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is sitting in the back row in the middle. He has a dark red tie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will so reflect the identification of the accused by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, are you absolutely certain that this is the man who participated in the beating of you which took place on the hangar floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I do your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will recess early. We will stand in recess until 2.30, please. (1.00 p.m.). (Luncheon Adjournment) (2.30 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Cross-Examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, from what you have told us, it seems that these three serious beatings that you suffered occurred within the period of a week, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first beating was largely the responsibility of Dragan, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Nikica Janjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Nikica Janjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Janjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Dragan's other name is what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know any other name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be Dragan Vujic or something beginning with the letter "V"? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have heard something about it in the camp, but that does not seem to be true. There seems to be another surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. The reason why I put that to you is from the statement that you gave to the Prosecution. You gave, if you may remember, a number of names for Dragan that began with "V", is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but then I pointed out that I was not sure ---

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- what was involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, does it seem to be that it was your impression it could have been a name beginning with "V"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure. That was just guessing by inmates, but the fact is that he is related to Nedzo Delic, that he had worked for him that he had worked in the restaurant in Omarska, in Europa, and the other Europa in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His identity is easy to establish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The second beating that took place upon you, again Nikica Janjic was involved, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dragan involved in that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the second beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The third beating that took place took place in the large building before you on that model which we call the hangar, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had been recovering from those previous beatings in a room that you have identified by calling room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was unable to see from here, but I believe you pointed to a fairly large room in the middle of the model on the first floor, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You had been in that room for how many days before the third beating took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About five or six days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably, in that period of time you were in an appalling physical state with bad and serious injuries to your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with no medical treatment to restore you and relieve pain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there a number of other men in that room in a similar condition at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a large number of injured people. I cannot tell you for sure how many because I was in a corner, but I know that there were many such people similar to me, beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That room that you were in, room 15, were there many people also confined into that space?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several hundred people, maybe 300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably as well, many of them were suffering the same bad conditions in relation to their eating, sanitation and drinking that you had experienced? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is something that you would never have experienced in your life before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Something that probably drove you to the limit of your endurance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the limit of my endurance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position that you were being kept within in this room, presumably, suffered from lack of ventilation and would have been a room that was baking in the sun because of the weather at the time, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How can you bake in the sun in a closed room?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We heard from one witness about the outside temperature being so hot that the rooms in that building because of the tin roof had an almost oven effect and caused the conditions to be very hot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was hot, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasion of the third beating, you were still in room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you had much opportunity to obtain food during the period of the previous week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not go out to eat. I ate what I was given by my friends, a piece of bread in their pockets. That is all I ate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably, that was to avoid further contact with guards as well as because of your strength, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have described being in a corner of room 15. Would that have been a corner furthest from the door which you indicated on the model was the door how you actually entered the room, or was it a corner nearer the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the right-hand corner and the left-hand corner was further away from the door than the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the opposite end of the room though to the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter the main door, you pass the first part of the room. On the one side there are showers, on the other side wash basins. You go into this part of the room. I was lying on the right-hand side in the corner. So the left-hand corner is further away than the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that gives us an indication as to where you were. You said that it was later in the afternoon around 6 o'clock that you heard a voice from the entrance to the door. Did that voice call your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then go down the room to the door to see the person who called your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that Nikica or another guard or someone else? Can you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Dragan, the one we talked about a while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan was standing there, and was he on his own or with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On his own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then did he take you down the stairs to the ground floor of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you at all what was going to happen, why he had called your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any feelings in your own mind as to why he called your name then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I had experienced -- I had experience with him, I knew what to expect roughly, but I prayed to God that he would kill me so that I would not be tortured any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when abouts during your stay in Omarska this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the middle of June. I cannot be sure of two or three days, but that is the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course not. I understand it would seem from what you are saying if it was in the middle of June that you may have been in the camp for some two-and-a-half weeks by then, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, about two weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left that room and went down the stairs with Dragan and you said that he was the only guard there, were there other guards, nothing to do with this incident, around on the stairs or nearby as you went down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I went down, there was nobody, but when he told me to go towards the hangar I saw the group in the hangar, I saw the group which would torture me later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have referred there to the hangar. We know that this was a mining complex and we know what this building was used for when it was working as a mine. Can you tell us what was actually in the hangar at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some parts of probably dump trucks, lorries. I think there was a dump truck further down on the left-hand side as you enter the hangar, left of the canal. It was not important to me at the time what was there. The only thing I was concerned with was the criminals when I entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it used at all at this time for the holding of any of the prisoners within Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which area do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I ask this because we have heard evidence that at some stage, I do not know when, the prisoners were kept in an area of this hangar, and what I am asking you is if at that time when you went down whether that was the case then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: True, but at that time there had not been -- by that time there had not been any inmates in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what appears to have been within it was equipment connected with lorries and the use of those lorries, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into the hangar, you have described what you say is the group of criminals. How many people did you see there in this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not get round to counting them, but there were between seven and 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragan had brought you down from the upstairs of the building. Did you have to walk with any help or what was your physical condition in relation to how you could move at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was still able to stand on my feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that that would have been though with quite a degree of pain and discomfort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Those various beatings that you had received on those other two occasions had been beatings, from what you have told us, over the whole of your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the group of men as wearing different kinds of clothes, but that they were all military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us what different kinds of military uniforms those clothes would have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them wore multi-coloured uniforms, we called them multi-colours, and others had grey olive uniforms of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "multi-coloured uniforms", is that camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of them wear berets, hats of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did, but at that time it did not make any difference whether he had a hat on or not. We were not interested in that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just asking you this to get an idea of the various kinds of clothing that were being worn. Can you remember any particular kinds of hats or berets, if there were any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had hats, caps. They dressed as they pleased. They did not look like an army. It looked like a band of wanton people. We could see from the start that there was no commanding hierarchy, no army, no men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that Dragan was the person who was in charge of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my impression, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had a military uniform, you said, with a white belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the others have a similar colour belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember at this time, nor did I try very hard to observe that. I was -- I did not believe that I would come out of the camp and especially that a day would come that I could testify to being there. If I had been aware of that, I would have remembered and observed more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, and do not take any of these questions as being a criticism of you. I am asking them as part of my job, you understand? Can you remember the kind of footwear perhaps that was being worn, whether they were boots or other form of ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly military boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that do you mean the black military boot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the military boot of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you see any weapons there amongst the men, and by that I mean guns or rifles or machine guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They mostly wore automatic weapons and pistols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "wore" automatic weapons, do you mean they had them with them or they were actually on their bodies in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly had them in their hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were down there with these men, did you notice if there were any other prisoners that you could see within the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was there I did not notice any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the focus of attention of the group? They were not doing anything to anyone else, was it just you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not notice that. I did not notice anybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This room, the hangar, was it lit at all? What were the lighting conditions within it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any lighting. It was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. We can see on that model that there are what I would call roller doors -- I do not know if that translates -- but shutters that go up and down, were they up or down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not notice those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Within that group when you gave evidence this morning you said that Dule Tadic was a member of that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name any of the other people who made up that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was another guy who in the first time I was beaten stood in the doorway holding an automatic rifle in his hands so that I would not escape through the door, I noticed him; that Dusko and there was Dragan, others, I did not really notice them except those I knew, but I had the impression that all the guards were there. Guards who were on duty there, I did not notice them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one you referred to as also being present the first time you were beaten who was in the door with his rifle to stop you escaping, did you know his name at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a guard at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any guards there from the camp in the hangar at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, and they would mostly be admitted in, the guards would stay outside and then they indulged in orgies with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because Dragan whom you have mentioned, was he actually a guard at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken into that hangar by Dragan. You told us that he started hitting you with a baton as you were going down the steps. Was that the first series of blows on this occasion that you felt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he began beating me as I was coming down the stairs when he directed me towards the hangar. That is when he started dealing blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was giving this treatment to you and it was coming upon injuries that you had already suffered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the bottom of the stairs, how did you get into the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I perhaps did not ask that very clearly but there are big doors, are there not, with glass in them, am I right about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a glass door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have to open that yourself or did he open it for you and let you through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was open. Yes, it was open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You entered the hangar. Did he continue beating you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards that group and then the group took over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The group, you have identified them as a group which implies that they were very much together in close proximity, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you entered the doors, whereabouts exactly were the group positioned, can you remember how far from the doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, a couple of metres inside the hangar, about halfway in the middle of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. There are some canals that we know of within this hangar, maybe three or four. Do you know what I am talking about when I refer to them? I did not hear any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was none.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what I am talking about when I refer to the canals within the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Canals to repair dump trucks ---

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and lorries and things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Get underneath them, go into a sort of a pit. Do you know what I am talking about within that hangar? Did you see those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to see in relation to those pits whereabouts the men were? Were they on that side or a different part of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that half beyond the canals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Dragan, presumably, was the man who forced you towards them or did they come to meet you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went towards them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone talk to you or did the beating just start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not saying anything. They were simply cursing. During all those beatings always there were no conversations of any kind. They would curse at you because you were a Muslim and they would hit you. I mean, there was no conversation there. They would not let you. All they cared about, how to hit you in the most vulnerable spot, no talking. Just curses and noise, that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the way you describe it, it would be right to say that it was the whole group that was involved in attacking you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the whole group, some probably hit me more times, sometimes less, but I had no time to count how many times who each of them hit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again when you came into that hangar, as you have told us, you were on your feet, you were walking, but you were being hit by Dragan, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he behind you hitting you or to the side or front hitting you? Can you tell us whereabouts he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was hitting you on your back, presumably? Was it on the back of your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the neck, head, shoulders -- that is where he hit me most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself had a bandaged head because of the appalling head injuries you had suffered the time of the previous beatings, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The distance that he hit you towards this group was how much, are you able to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six metres, perhaps 10, I do not know. Five or six metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the group immediately start hitting you like Dragan was doing? I will repeat the question because I do not think there is a translation for the witness. Did the group start hitting you like Dragan had been doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, they beat me, Dragan used only batons and they used their rifle butts, feet, rods, but basically with their feet. Those karateists, they were the ones, perhaps they were doing their exercises -- training with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presumably, you would have been kicked or hit to the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not remain on your feet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The length of time that this continued for, are you able to tell us in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about 20 minutes, 15, 20 -- it looked like eternity to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to ask you about is Dusko Tadic, when you first say that you came to know of him and his name. When do you say you first came across him, if you like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew of his existence. I have known it for some 10 years. As I have already said, I knew him from sight. I knew that he was Dule. I did not know his full name, but I knew he was Dule. I knew his family name was Tadic, that he lived in Kozarac and that he was practising karate and coaching karate. I knew he was no good, that he was a trouble maker. He used to come to Prijedor on the street where my business was, and there he was beaten once by Remzo, Cero and those friends of mine. I knew all that went on in that street, since my coffee bar was the best known and the most popular in Prijedor and very many young people came there, so that I know him, you see. For 10 years I have known who he was, what he was, where he came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are talking about being aware of him, is that right, for some 10 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you answer the question because there has to be a translation. When you say you saw him in the hangar on that occasion when you received the third beating, are you able to describe what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to my mind, like everybody else when he was wearing a military uniform. I remember that, simply I recognised him immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you recognised him, was there anything about his appearance that you could describe how he looked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have just said briefly, he was not alone so that I would look at him only. I was looking at them, at that group of seven or 10 people, so that he was the only one whose name I knew from that group. Dragan's name I learnt in the camp and that other one who took part in former beatings, I still do not know his name to this day, so it is quite natural that his name stuck in my mind. But before that, I have never had any trouble with him before. At that time I was not as scared of him as thinking of Dragan and what Dragan was going to do to me. I believe he could not recognise me because from the previous beating, my mine, my face was all disshaped, misshapen, and when the one upstairs had called out my name, I guess that he did not have the faintest idea who they were talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You rightly say that you were not concentrating on one person because what was happening to you involved the whole group of seven or 10, that is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not being politely taken into this room by Dragan; you were being hit by him from behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what had happened to you in those previous days, you were not in your normal physical condition, that is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Physically, no, naturally, but mentally I was well enough to notice that Dule Tadic was there and that he was practising some blows on me. More him, I cannot even remember those other faces because they meant nothing to me. I did not recognise anyone of them. They must have been the population from Omarska and perhaps other villages there who never came down, so I could not know them nor could they know me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you recollected Dule Tadic because the name stuck in your mind, it is right to say that you have talked about things with other people when you were in the camp then as well as in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to object to a mischaracterisation of the evidence. The witness did not say he recollected Dule Tadic because of the name. He said that he recognised him for that reason and did not know the other names, and so it is natural that he would remember Mr. Tadic. Counsel is building in a mischaracterisation into that question.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is how I recall the testimony. I suppose we could have it turned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I apologise and I am sure the Court will allow me to start again and put whatever I should put correctly. You say that the name stuck in your mind, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The face features.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the face and features, had the face or features changed in any way from how you had seen Dusko Tadic from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time they had not changed at all. They are changed now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the person who was hitting you then had a look, an appearance, as you say it was Dusko Tadic, he had not changed in his appearance from when you had known him from before, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was him, I was not having any halucinations. I did not have to think any. I am positive. I was quite sure it was him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, what I suggest to you is that, in fact, what was happening to you was so extreme that it was difficult for you to accurately recognise Dusko Tadic and be right about it, do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was strong enough to recognise him, to know that it was he and not forced to think whether it was he or not and that I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refer to your mental state, but you had suffered appalling deprivation in that time in Omarska in terms of your health, physical condition, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, but I was, I still had enough of my wits about to know that it was he, that I could not make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because what I am putting to you is this, that in fact it was someone who looked like him but it was not him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was he.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This name is something that you have picked up because others were talking about it in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why should I? I knew him more than those other people. There was nothing -- they could hear it from me, not I from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have never had a conversation with Dusko Tadic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have never sat at a table with Dusko Tadic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in a coffee, in the coffee bar just, but not together because we had no reason to strike any friendships even before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Miso Danicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, I have one question to ask you. Did alcohol play any part in the camp as far as the guards were concerned or those who came in and beat you? Did they seem to be drunk or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, alcohol played a tremendous role there. They were almost all drunk and regularly, day in, day out, and we were blackmailed. They would take a man, put a pistol in his mouth and say, "Get me 1,000 marks in", I do not know, "within 15 or 20 minutes or we will kill him", and of course we had to find that money, whether we knew the man or not. I mean, those who managed somehow to bring the money in, we collected 10 marks, 15 marks, it depended, but towards the end we stopped giving it because we knew that they were going to kill us all, so we thought, "What is the use? He will only suffer more so let them", and then they became even stricter. They were requesting, I do not know, 230 marks and then they dropped the price to a crate of beer because they simply could not do without beer or drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guards have a meeting room, a common room, where they drank or did you see them drink or do you know anything of how they ate? Where did they eat, for instance, the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They do not know it -- yes, while I was in this room behind the restaurant, here where this tap is, there was a van and the door of this van was always open, the rear door could always be open, and there was a machine gun directed at this door through which we entered behind the tap, and they drank there non-stop bottles of brandy, of cognac, crates of beer. What they ate? What do I know what those scum ate -- pork, must be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One other question, you spent some time on the pista in the open air?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of a night would you sleep on the pista or were you always taken into the so-called restaurant at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first four or five days I spent nights on the pista. There was a machine gun positioned up here on this roof, and in the evening it was sighted on us, it was aimed at us, and after some five or six days there was a shower so that they would not get soaked and better to keep us under control, they forced us into the restaurant. We would spend the night there until the day break, and at day break they would force us out into the pista. On the pista there were those puddles of water after the rain, but who cared? Each one had to take his place, whether wet or dry, and lie down again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question I wanted to ask you is I take it the pista was floodlit at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was lit around it, not where we were. As far as I can remember, there were some lights here and there, but they had a good view. There was a wall here and there was this machine gun. Joja, one of those, I do not know who he is, and he always kept it aimed at us, so we had no chance, not even a theoretical chance, to attempt an escape or a rebellion or something because I think it would not take a minute to kill us all and sometimes we were 700 or 600, 800 of us, so that we had no chance whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Beganovic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. I wish to thank your Lordships. I am glad that I did. I hope I helped you. I tried to as much as I could. Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, who will your next witness be? Mr. Tieger, you will call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, the next witness is Senad Muslimovic. SENAD MUSLIMOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you take the oath that is being handed to you, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Would you be seated? Examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Senad Muslimovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic, you may want to move a little bit away from the microphone when you speak. What year were you born?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also raised in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in 1981.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war exactly where in Prijedor did you live, not the address but what part of town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An area that boarded on the centre of the city called Puharska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic, is it correct that you come from a rather well-known family in Bosnia, in particular, because of your brother's success in the music business?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope that that was the case. I think that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother is a very popular and well-known folk singer in Bosnia, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked in the music business with him and worked together with him when he toured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you spent a great deal of time outside of Prijedor as a result of your work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the tensions which preceded the actual conflict in Prijedor and in Bosnia, did people in Prijedor tend to distinguish between who was Muslim and who was Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally did not. I think others were not able to do so either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have Serb friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had many more Serbian friends than if I can say Muslim friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in part of because of the nature of your work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not be able to tell you exactly. I had such friends, that happens to be the case. I had those friends and I was fond of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to distinguish between a Muslim and a Serb based on their physical appearance, based on their face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is impossible for me. Maybe someone in the world might do that but I could not. I could never do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to your work in the music business, did you also have your own grocery business in Prijedor before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of the tensions which occurred before the conflict actually began, did you send your wife and children away to Slovenia for safety at some point before May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you yourself in Prijedor when the cleansing of Prijedor town began on May 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you seized or arrested the following day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen what happened to your home before that, before you were captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had happened to it, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I watched everything from the part of a town which was opposite my house and called Percani. I was staying with a friend called Dzevad Deomic. I was in his bedroom watching. There were fires here and there in the area of Puharska. At one point from one part of a road down from my house, a tank came out and started moving in the direction of Banja Luka. That is the easiest explanation, if I say in the direction of Banja Luka, because the road connected Bosanski Novi and Banja Luka. They passed my house. I would not be able to tell you how many metres, but I know that they crossed the bridge next to my house. Then they came back and then they trained the barrel towards my house and fired at it. That is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we call up on the monitor Z5-35? Looking at the monitor, Mr. Muslimovic, do you recognise what is shown on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly that is my house when it was, the way it looked when it was built about 10 or 12 years ago. During the war it was even bigger and more beautiful. It was my family house which belongs to my father, to my brother, to my mother. We lived there together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It included the entire structure shown in the picture in addition to a portion which had not yet been built at the time this picture was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question, would you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your family house consisted of the entire structure shown in this picture, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but 10 years ago, maybe even longer than that, but just before the war it was much bigger and more beautiful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that in I am not quite sure what form we can do so. I would actually like to return the actual photograph to the witness, if possible, so if it is technically feasible to capture an image of what is on the screen now or certainly a photographic copy.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Take it wherever it is, retrieve it and make a copy of it. What Exhibit number will this be then so that we have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Exhibit 253, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 253?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. 253 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Miss Sutherland suggests that perhaps we could make this 253A and the following photograph can be 253B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 253A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we also now call up on the monitor Z5-34? (To the witness): Mr. Muslimovic, do you recognise this picture and is this a picture of your home after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender this, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 253B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. (To the witness): Mr. Muslimovic, after you were arrested or seized on May 31st where were you first taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the police station in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you struck or beaten when you were being transported to the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived was there a group or cordon of Serbian police waiting who also beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the SUP was there an attempt or a threat of an execution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not every day but every other day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day you were taken to the SUP, were you lined up for execution at some point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you lined up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was lined up in the courtyard, if I can call it, of the SUP behind the main entrance on the other side next to the wall. On the left-hand side, there was a door. That is where I was put together for the act that they had planned to carry out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were on the other side next to a wall, what was the condition of that wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was smeared with blood and there were pot marks that looked like bullet scars, but at that moment nobody paid enough attention to decide 100 per cent what sort of hole it was. When I was placed there, the only thing, the only things I could see was the blood and the holes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What occurred to stop the execution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a split moment, after a very short moment, from the main room of the SUP building a gentleman who was a stranger to me came out. I can call him a gentleman. He said that this cannot happen, that we are loyal citizens of that town and nobody can do us any harm. But, however, it went on for a certain time and he placed some people to watch me like nothing would happen, but it lasted only the time, during the time that he was in the doorway. As soon as he went back, we were beaten again, not as badly as later, but there were blows on the head with the rifle, just beating, until a situation materialised in which I was saved. They usually beat people until someone came along who did not like his friend to be beaten without any reason. That is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were held in the SUP, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the incident in the courtyard (which seemed very long to me, like a year although it must have been short), we were taken to a room and then from that room we were taken again to the courtyard, if I can call it that, where we were delivered many, many blows on all sides. You could not observe who was doing it. We had to bow down and protect our head as much as possible. We were lined up there, there might have been five, six or seven. I did not look around very much in front of me or around me. I did not have enough courage to do so. There was also alternative beating until they took us to the room, the room, to the premises of the main SUP. If we passed a soldier, that soldier would hit you with a rifle or kick you or you would just get a slap in the face. We went through the SUP, went out. We were thrown, not taken, into the bus, we were thrown on to a bus, which already had people on it. That is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that bus take you to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, how long were you held in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question? How long? Is it a question about my time in Keraterm or the time the trip took?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, your time in Keraterm, how long were you actually held in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about -- a day lasted as long as a year, sometimes it was faster and very slow, but I think seven or 10 days, but I would not say -- I do not think it was 10 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of Keraterm were you held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Still dark that night, we were chased out of the bus and put in the first room which was located at the corner of the building. I do not know what the purpose of the room was, but it was at the corner itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were held in Keraterm were prisoners called from your room at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear what was happening to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to hear, yes. It was not small things when you hear a man screaming, yelling, howling, roaring, it is hard to imitate that under normal conditions. That is what I heard, screams, shrieks, moans. That is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the prisoners who were called from the room return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Generally, it is hard to say what number, you always expect to be the next one so you do not think about numbers. Generally, there were more people called out than those who returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of those who returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know, from our point of view, they looked like they had been wounded. Sometimes they looked like walking corpses. It seems impossible, but that is what they looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Keraterm were you called out for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kinds of questions were you asked during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How should I tell you? The first question was, "Where is your money? Where did you hide your money? Where are your weapons? Why did you help any of the Parties?" But, however, I have never been a member of any political party. "How much money did your brother give for this one, for that one?" Everything was revolved around, "Where is your money? Where were you that day, on such-and-such a day, at such-and-such a moment?" If I can say so, those questions were stupid to me. That is all. I had to say where I had left gold, money, that I did not have because I had invested everything. I did not have any capital because I had invested everything, but all the time I was asked for money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the interrogators were not completely satisfied with your answers, what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would say, "We have better methods, you will admit eventually".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken out of Keraterm at some point for a short time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took you out of Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken by a man who was called by everybody in the camp Zigic, and whom everybody knew by that nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did this man Zigic take you out of camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can claim that because I was escorted by them to my house, but first they told me to go into Halid's house and look for money and gold, and then they went to my house and told me to look for it, but I did not have any. You know what happens after that; beatings, torture and then taking me back to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So first they took you to your brother's house and then to your house looking for valuables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the period of ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- of time you indicated, were you taken from Keraterm to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of Omarska were you held after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was placed in room No. 15. That is what I heard the number was. There was no number on it, but that is what it was called, room No. 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic, do not take off your headphones just yet, but I will ask you to get up and point out on the model in front of you -- you may use the pointer to your right, if you wish -- where the room in which you were held which you knew as room 15 was. You may want to remove your headphones when you walk over and point it out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I begin?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. If you could also put on those headphones when you get over there in case there is something else I need to ask you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is that all?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If you could first point to room 15, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the numbers which are on the floor of the area which comprises room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B7, B23 and B8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you can return to your seat. What did room 15 consist of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean? I did not understand the question. Are you referring to the material it was made of or what it was composed of?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question. Did you have a particular place in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was in a shower booth. It was so big that two of us had to sleep in it and you know roughly how big it is. Sometimes there were three of us sleeping in one shower booth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we call up Z3, 15-13, please? Mr. Muslimovic, do you recognise what is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those some of the shower booths in room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your place on this side or on the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My place cannot be seen on this side. It is on the left-hand side and my place was on the left-hand side in the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this as Exhibit 254.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 254 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if you would tell the witness again to keep back from the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic, if I could ask you to move back a little bit from the microphones? They are quite sensitive and they will be able to pick up your voice. Toward the latter part of your imprisonment in Omarska, did you manage to get into a room in the restaurant and away from room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did, but only towards the end of my stay in the camp, towards the end of the hell that was taking place there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do so because you had been told you were on a liquidation list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were in room 15 were prisoners regularly called out at night from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did many of them disappear after they were called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many of those who were called out never returned to our room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about those who did return, what was their physical condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Walking corpses, wounded, injured. We cannot describe that, but we can just say a wounded man is returning. We could not see which parts of the body were wounded, but he was walking like he had just been run over by a car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were beatings a regular occurrence at Omarska, beatings of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When would those things occur? What would prisoners be doing when beatings would happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. Under what circumstances would those beatings take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were called out, taken out and beaten up. That was mostly late, in the late afternoon and then on through the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about during other times when prisoners were going to their meal or were going to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, when we went to our meals that was the daily event. If you got away without any beating, that was great luck. When you went to the toilet, you had to keep from going because you never knew what criminal was there at the door. Daily, wherever you went out of the room, you expected to be beaten and if you were not beaten, that was just a piece of luck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to going to meals. What kind of food did prisoners receive when they went to meals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were given a meal a day, sometimes no meal, and most frequently the last inmates did not get anything, the first got something, so they returned without having anything. The meal was the kind that I would never serve anybody, not even my greatest enemy I would not allow to eat that. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am about to move on to a new area.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Today we are going to adjourn at 5 o'clock so we will stand in recess though for 20 minutes. (4.00 p.m.). (Short adjournment) (4.20 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you. Mr. Muslimovic, did you know anyone named Dule Tadic before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Omarska did other prisoners point out to you a man they said was named Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen that man before Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten by this man in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had two direct collisions with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the beatings, did you see him in Omarska at other times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him in front of the kitchen and in front of the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
