utterances.text: How many times did you see him by the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About two times, I should say, twice, two or three -- twice, that is safer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him by the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were moving towards the kitchen. We were going for lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you see him by the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also about two times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him by the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the window in the room in which I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May of this year did investigators show you a book of photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I did not hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. In May of this year did investigators show you a book of photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time before you were shown the book of photographs, had you seen a picture of the person in camp you knew as Dule Tadic in any newspapers or television or from any other source?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to look at the photographs in the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not getting the interpretation. I do not hear anything. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. You finally heard the question and you were asked to look at the photographs in the book. Were you asked to see if there was anyone you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you whose pictures were in the book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look at the photographs in the photo book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After looking at the photographs in the photo book had you seen the photograph of someone you were sure you recognised from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the person who beat you on two occasions and whom you had been told was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign and date the back of the photograph of the person you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown which should be marked for identification as Exhibit 255?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I have a look at it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looks like it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the book of photographs you were shown, Mr. Muslimovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does your signature and the date appear on the back of the photograph you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I would have to take a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 255 for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand there is a running objection to the use of the photospread book.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will note that objection. It will be overruled. Exhibit 255 is admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Mr. Muslimovic, I would like to ask you about the first time you were beaten by this man. Did that occur after an interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the interrogation conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the room above the kitchen to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten during that interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course and quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the interrogation was over what path did you take back to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same path that I got there, down the stairs and from the kitchen to the -- from the white house to the kitchen and then naturally upstairs to room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you walked toward the entrance to the hangar, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, each one of us looked for some comfort and trying to see someone, to greet someone, to say "hello" to someone. Each one of us could be called out and not returned. Each one had his own story to tell, and I accompanied by blows from the kitchen, blows I received with an electric cord, I walked to the corner, what should I call it, a hangar, or a building, the one that is in front of me. There I was for a while let alone. The guard went around me and came in front. Of course, I had to follow him, but I took a glance. My head had to be down but I did steal a look, and there were about five, six, 10 people in front there. Of course I do not know how many because I did not dare look for longer, it was too dangerous, but you were looking for some comfort to save your life, then it is not as dangerous. It is more dangerous when you know there is no escape. Of the people who stood there -- there were about five or six or seven of them, I did not count them -- I recognised Kecema, Dusko, or perhaps I thought that he could be the one who could perhaps help me to end as a dead man, but from what I could see he gave no sign of coming near me, coming to me, saying, "How are you? Where are you?" or something. He was just walking up and down. When I saw that, I simply felt he would not help me. When I was near the door, not quite at the door but near it, I cast a last look, hoping that that man who I believed might help me, would do something, anything, but I could no longer see him. He was not in the line of my eyes, and I only heard a man saying, "Oh, well, I know this one. He has got broad shoulders" and he started towards me. I hurried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the group that Dusko Kecema was with? Can you point it out with the long pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that grassy area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may be seated. Do you know who he was with at that time or did you see any of the people at that point who he was with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I used to see some of those people, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the remark was made by someone that he knew this one who has broad shoulders and you hurried toward the hangar, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started towards the hangar and I did try to hurry because somehow I did feel some danger was imminent and I reached the door, the entrance door to the staircase, not the room, but the staircase and there I felt a blow which made me fall down on my hands in the direction of the stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you fell down in the direction of the stairs, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I fell on my hands and I remained in that posture. My hands and my feet were on the ground. I was not lying down exactly, but I was like that, and he came from behind my back and got me by my hair and was pushing me left and right, shoving me left and right, and in this driving, I do not know what else to call it, I had to lift my hands and at one point I faced the exit doors from this area where the stairs were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, after you first fell to your hands and knees, someone came from behind you and grabbed you by the hair and pulled you back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Left and right, up and down, around, as if trying to shake something. I do not know how to describe it. He grabbed me by the hair. He turned me to the right, to the left but very roughly, very strongly. It was painful, of course. After that shuffling right and left, up and down, I found myself facing the exit door but on my knees still.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he grabbed you by the hair, were you able to see who had grabbed you by the hair and did you recognise who that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course the gentleman on the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you found yourself facing the exit door but still on your knees, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment I saw a man holding a beret. My head was still pulled back so that I had to watch it, and it was right in front of my eyes ---

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak up a little, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and the man holding that beret ---

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- told me to kiss it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- would you speak up a little bit? It is very difficult to know just how far; we tell you to move forwards and then we tell you to move back. I have the same problem. But speak up a bit and if you have a problem, let us know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I was staring at that beret. There was a badge on it which we all knew. I did not really try to see the colours and all that, but at that moment I saw a Kokarda. I was ordered to kiss it, which I refused and after a little while, a kick from a person who was standing across me and holding this Kokarda hit me, so that simply as he hit me I fell against that Kokarda and it cut my lip, and I was bleeding. This was followed by a series of blows up and down, left and right. You did not know where they came from. The important thing was that you were receiving those blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the man who had the Kokarda and who kicked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know his name. I know his nickname was Saponja, but whether that was his real name or a nickname, I do not know. I do not think that Saponja is a name, but I believe it is a nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the series of blows following Saponja's kick to your mouth, what was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the blow a series of blows followed and I received a blow in the head like this. I could not see what it was, with what it was, but the blow was so strong that I stumbled forward. I fell to that posture and I remained there because as I stumbled the most important thing was to hide one's head because everything else was less painful. But there were blows on my arms and everywhere, so that I was trying to protect my head slightly. At one point I felt that my arms were blocked, that somebody was standing on my hands and I could not move either right or left. Then a series of blows in the head followed and then some object was thrown. I was not watching it, but I know it hurt. Then it came against my back, so one expects it to hit you, but how that object reached my back I do not know. At any rate, I was in this posture and there was this object, that thing falling down on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you struggle to get away and were you successful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, a whole day of interrogation and beating you could not call it interrogation, beating, I really was powerless, but somehow I summoned up strength because I thought it was the end, I thought I would not get out alive, that that is where my end would happen. As they were still hitting me left and right and everywhere, somehow I managed to pull my hands...hands free and in this fury I managed to run up the stairs. I did it. I did it. I managed to get away and reach, I cannot understand how, but I did manage to reach the top of the stairs where there was a guard with a rifle aimed at me. I did not care any longer whether he would fire, perhaps it would have been easier. I simply pushed him away. At that moment I felt that it would be much easier for me if he fired because if I went back it would be the same. As it was I thought it would hurt less. So the door was open, well, I cannot say it was unlocked, neither it was closed, I think the door was ajar. So, as I was thrusting forward, as I pushed him away I just got into the room, and that must have been some divine force, I do not know what it was, I cannot describe it. At any rate, I entered and I felt safer. What did it mean "safer"? But I was among other people. I was not alone. If anything was going to happen then I was not alone. I was with them. I do not know how. I was not moving normally, walking normally, but at the entrance I was passing through the door and I received another strong blow in the back. So that, I do not know how to put it, I stumbled, I staggered and I then staggered on to this area, to this room, where I used to sleep, where on one hand there were the shower booths and on the other side a trough, a concrete trough, and I somehow managed to get in and that is where I fell down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone follow you into the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From that moment when I was walking, while I was still moving, I did not know that, but as I fell by the trough I heard a bullet and I thought it was the bullet intended for me. That is how it sounded, echoing, "Nobody approach me, I will kill anyone who comes close", and then I realised he was in, that he was in that room where we were. I heard, "Don't move, don't turn around, I will kill anyone who moves." Then the voices were getting further and furtherer away. It was not as loud as when they were next to me, as the first moment it appeared, as sounding as if it was right next to me, and the door closed. I tried to stand up, to straighten up by this trough because that was not the place where I used to be before. I did straighten up but I fell down again. As far as I can remember, it was Mr. Alic, I believe it was Mirso Alic, I am not absolutely sure but I think it was him, he came to me and how I reached the place where I used to be before I do not know, from the trough to my usual place. I do not know. I know I fell down and when I came to I realised I was in my place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you heard a bullet. Is that the sound of a bullet being fired or a bullet being chambered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I heard a regular being chambered, a rifle uncocked. Perhaps I said a bullet, but what I heard was a rifle being cocked. Well, I guess the sound was very loud. It sounded very loud. It sounded as if it was right by my ear that sound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long after this first beating did the second beating involving the man you knew as Dule occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very difficult to speak about time, but I think it must have been a week, not more than that, perhaps a day or two more or less, but about a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in room 15 that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time of the day did the incident occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened late in the afternoon. It was still light, but I did not have a watch. I do not know the date. It was impossible to remember. I could not be bothered really. I simply did not want to think, but it was late in the afternoon and it was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a prisoner called out from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Emir Beganovic was called out could you hear the sounds of a beating coming from downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sounds reached that area where I was, but not so loudly, not as if it was in the next room or in my room. They came from the outside. One could hear them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometime after that were you called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the voice that was calling you out coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the room and did you get up and go toward the entrance door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the first time, but the second time when the same voice came I had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a Serb soldier outside the door when you left the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there another Serb waiting for you down the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That man was stood at the bottom of the stairs, perhaps a metre, half a metre. Generally speaking, he was standing by the stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that person wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I remember is the white belt, the white belt and military uniform naturally, but this white belt stuck in my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the man with the white belt stop you or let you pass initially?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, at that moment when I came near him he let me pass by and stayed behind my back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I turned right, it was two or three steps, so I started and there was a man with a rifle who said, "No, no, there", and immediately a blow from the back followed and then so on and so forth, I was accompanied by blows. From the left and from the right, I did not know where they were coming from. You had to cover your head to protect yourself, so you protected yourself up there and then they hit you below. So there were blows from the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak up or come closer to the microphone? We barely here him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Muslimovic, I will ask you to move your chair a little closer to the microphone again, if you do not mind. Were you hit or pushed toward the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a bit struck. The strongest ones were in the back and those were the ones who pushed me. That was from the left, from the right and then one from the back, so that I had to stagger forward. That is how the blows directed me to this door, not towards the exit but towards the interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the interior part of the hangar, that is the hangar floor, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not enter, that is putting it very mildly. Under those blows there was force which directed me that way. Then came questions, not questions but orders, "Take off your jacket", so I took off my jacket which was of a coffee colour. I gave it to the person who had met me at the stairs and, of course, he began to search through it, to frisk it. It was not much, but he began to look there and he was cursing and saying, "Where's your money?" and curses and filthy language. I was not thinking much about that. I was wondering whether they would hit me again. I felt and I saw this jacket. It was low and my head was down, but I was trying to look like this, and I felt how this jacket was thrown away as if behind the back. There was nothing in it for sure. Then questions ensued, "Where's your money? What kind of a mortar do you have?" and things like that. I mean such provocative questions that you just look at him, I mean, you know, someone asks you, "Where's your tank?" I mean you cannot hide a tank. It was like that. It was so incredible. If he had asked me some normal questions perhaps I might have thought about them, but the questions were such that there was nothing you could reply. So you just kept silent and question was accompanied, was followed by a blow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a group of Serbs there at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. Not in a group, but when you are hit and your head goes right or left or up and down and every time it moves you are bound to see somebody. They were all over, in front and behind and to the left, because whenever he hit you you could not keep your posture, you changed simply the posture. Whenever you looked they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they beating you with, what sorts of objects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rifles, electrical cords, soldiers' boots which was very, very heavy, perhaps heavier than the gun, a baseball bat. This is what I could see and feel on my back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point did you end up held against a dumper tyre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After this series of blows which followed, mostly from the gentleman with white slings and white belt, and others too of course but more often than not from that gentleman, I could not see anything. You hear, but you just do not see. All is dark, all is black. I do not know what to call it, but at that moment I did not see anything regardless of whether I had my eyes open or not. I heard again a noise, shouts, but I could not understand, I could not distinguish. When I realised that I was able to see something around me, I was already straightened up and I could not fall down because my arms were in that position and fixed. So I assumed I had been tied because it was impossible for a man to stand like that. My head was bent down. As the seconds were passing by I was recovering my consciousness more and more and I realised that I was tied to a tyre which was bigger than I. I did not turn to see what kind of a tyre it was. I could not. One could see while hit that it was a tyre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after you were held against that tyre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was always accompanied by blows, a series of blows and noise, curses, always swearing at mother, at religion, and they were practising blows. I was just a bat they used to practise blows. They practised them until I lost consciousness again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of blows did they practise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were mostly blows, how shall I say, I do not know how to put it. Most of the blows were with the foot, mostly with a foot. Naturally some came with a rifle or some with a bat, but they were mostly kicks with the foot, from the right and from left, and they hurt most here from the chin downward. Those were the kicks that I felt best. Everything else somehow I could endure easier than those kicks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the kicks from any particular person the strongest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Must be because those were the ones that I felt most and that they hurt most. I thought somehow when he hit me here I felt them in the back, as if they went right through. If somebody came with a rifle, that was fine with me. That was really very nice for me as compared with that kick. I mean, the word "fine" is not perhaps the best word, but I somehow felt easier when hit with the rifle or anything else than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it whose kicks were the strongest and most effective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gentleman whom I recognised in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Should I continue your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until Tuesday at 10.30. We will begin at 10.30 on Tuesday instead of 10 o'clock. (5.00 p.m.). (The court adjourned until Tuesday, 23rd July 1996)
